newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater figure Starr ordered to appear in court.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater figure Starr ordered to appear in court.

text.p: A judge Tuesday ordered Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth Starr to testify in the trial of President Clinton's former business partner, Susan McDougal, who is accused of embezzlement in a separate case.

Defence Attorney Mark Geragos said Starr had been subpoenaed Monday when he was in San Francisco, but had flown back to Washington and was not in Santa Monica for the scheduled start of McDougal's trial Tuesday.

Based on Geragos' request, Superior Court Judge Paul Flynn signed an order to force Starr to come to Santa Monica to testify in the trial. However, he stayed the order until May 22 to give Starr a chance to voluntarily attend.
Essentially, Geragos wants Starr to explain to the court why McDougal has been held in prison outside Los Angeles since Dec. 18, while most embezzlement case defendants are granted bail.
"(Starr's) got, number one, all kinds of documents that are essential to her defence," Geragos told reporters.
"And number two, he needs to establish why she's being held, and why the orders the judge has issued (to transfer her to a local jail) are not being complied with."
He contends authorities are making it so uncomfortable for McDougal that she will change her mind and testify in the Whitewater probe.

McDougal has been locked in a 9-foot-by-5-foot cell at the Sybil Brand Institute for Women on federal contempt charges for refusing to tell Starr what she knows about Clinton's role in the Whitewater affair.
The affair, which has dogged Clinton's presidency, stems from the failure of the Madison Savings and Loan Association, which cost taxpayers an estimated $65 million.

Clinton, then governor of Arkansas, and his wife Hillary, entered into a partnership with James and Susan McDougal in the Whitewater real estate venture in 1978. Although their investment lost money, questions have arisen about whether funds for the project were siphoned from the savings and loan, which was also a McDougal holding.
Her husband, who cooperated with prosecutors, was sentenced to three years in prison for his part in Whitewater.

Judge Flynn has issued four orders for McDougal to be transferred to a less restrictive prison in Pasadena. Los Angeles County Sheriff Sherman Block has said McDougal is being held in a lockdown for all but 30 minutes a day for her own safety.
Geragos said she is on "murderer's row. That's the most punitive environment that they can keep her in."
In the Santa Monica case, which has nothing to do with Whitewater, Susan McDougal is charged with embezzling $150,000 from conductor Zubin Mehta.
She is accused of forging checks and obtaining a credit card in the name of Mehta's wife, Nancy, while she worked for the family.
